reference: The same coupled ODE system (CO2, O2, water vapour, trace contaminants, temperature, and the five accumulators) re-implemented independently in python from the model description and from the rate constants, crew rates and device characteristics read out of the page, integrated with scipy.integrate.solve_ivp (LSODA, rtol 1e-11, saturation handled as a constrained sub-system through a terminal event) — a different integrator family from the page fixed-step RK4. Grading is completed by invariants that owe nothing to either integration: the carbon and oxygen balances over the whole run, the analytic steady temperature, the ideal-gas closure, non-negativity, and the observed order of the scheme under step halving.
reference_citations: scipy 1.17.1, scipy.integrate.solve_ivp (LSODA: Adams/BDF with automatic stiffness switching and local error control) — the independent integrator.

The rate constants, crew metabolic rates and device characteristics are the page's own, read out of the file, so that the benchmark grades the mathematics rather than the choice of physiological data.

Data provenance of those rates, checked separately: NASA/SP-2010-3407/REV1 Human Integration Design Handbook and NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD, NASA/TP-2015-218570) give per crew member and day: 0.835 kg O2 consumed, 1.0 kg CO2 produced (respiratory quotient 0.87), about 1.9 kg metabolic water vapour and 2.5 kg drinking water; ASHRAE Standard 62.1 uses about 0.0052 L/s (19 L/h) of CO2 per sedentary adult.

Fourth-order Runge-Kutta truncation behaviour: E. Hairer, S. P. Norsett, G. Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations I, 2nd ed., Springer 1993, ch. II.1-II.3 (order conditions and the (h^4) global error of the classical scheme).
tolerance: Every displayed quantity is graded at 1e-7 relative plus a small absolute floor per quantity (1e-5 ppm CO2, 1e-7 kPa, 1e-6 K, 1e-6 % RH) for the near-zero cases. That is two orders of magnitude above the deviation actually observed against the adaptive reference (1e-9 or better) and two orders below anything that could reach the digits the page prints, so it grades the integration rather than the display. Carbon and oxygen balances are graded at 1e-9 relative for a sealed compartment, since the accumulators the page itself reports must close those balances exactly. The analytic steady temperature is graded at 0.02 K. The run at the step the page chooses must be step-converged: refining the step 16-fold must not move any displayed quantity by more than 1e-9 relative. The observed order of the scheme, measured where truncation is still visible (a reduced case with only the slow gas modes, steps of 225 s to 7200 s), must lie between 3.5 and 4.5. The saturated branch is the exception: there the surplus vapour is projected onto the saturation curve at the end of every step, which is a first-order splitting (measured order 1.00 over five halvings), so the saturating case is graded at 1e-4 relative — the deviation actually measured at the 10 s step the page uses is 1.8e-5 relative on the vapour pressure, 4.6e-5 K on the temperature and 1.3 g in 203 kg of condensate, three orders of magnitude below the resolution of anything the page prints — and the case additionally requires that deviation to fall linearly with the step, which is what proves the splitting consistent with the constrained solution.

provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/ga_cases.py from the sources this artifact cites; that generator was re-run against this tree on 2026-10-03 and its output compared with the deployed corpus leaf by leaf at 1 051 leaves, 0 differing, so no case reuses a stored ref and none carries ref_source "recorded".
crosscheck: Two independent statements about the same run are compared for every case: the trajectory from scipy.integrate.solve_ivp (adaptive, error-controlled) and the invariants computed from the page's own printed accumulators (carbon, oxygen, ideal-gas closure, saturation limit, store capacities). The two agree to 1e-9 relative or better everywhere except on the saturated branch, where the page's end-of-step projection is first order and leaves 1.8e-5 relative at its own step.
data_provenance: The benchmark grades the mathematics, not the physiological data: every rate constant, crew rate and device characteristic is the page's own, read out of the file. Checked separately against a cited source, the defaults are consistent with published values one at a time but not as a pair: 20 l/h of CO2 per person (20 °C, 101.325 kPa) is the ASHRAE 62.1 sedentary-adult figure (about 0.0052 L/s), 0.84 kg/d of O2 is the NASA baseline (0.835 kg/d), 0.09 kg/h of moisture and 75 W of sensible heat are ordinary light-activity figures, but the CO2/O2 pair implies a respiratory quotient of 0.760 where NASA BVAD pairs 1.0 kg CO2 with 0.835 kg O2 for 0.87. The page now shows that quotient with a note giving the physiological range and the NASA pair, and the benchmark grades both the value and its disclosure.
run_notes: Driven through the page DOM with Playwright; every case sets the input fields, calls the page's own recompute() and reads both the displayed values and the full-precision trace the page holds.
The reference is asked for the state at exactly the sample times the page reported, so nothing is interpolated on either side.

Step size: at the step the page picks (1.7-14.4 s here) all four test cases are converged to round-off — refining the step 16-fold moves nothing by more than 1e-12 relative. The fourth order of the scheme is therefore measured on a reduced case (crew production against the scrubber and the trace bed only) at steps of 225-7200 s, where the truncation error is still visible: observed order 4.29, 4.15, 4.07, 4.04, 4.02 over five halvings.

The saturated branch is first order by construction (end-of-step projection onto the saturation curve): observed order 1.00 over five halvings, deviation 1.8e-5 relative on the vapour pressure at the page's own step. This pass added that statement to the page limitations, to the model notes of the calculation record and to the manifest.

Before this pass the same 28 cases already passed: no numerical defect was found. What the pass changed is disclosure and interface — the 60 000-step cap is now reported when it binds (it did, silently, on two of the seven presets), the first-order saturated branch is stated, the respiratory quotient carries its physiological context, one result tile carried the label of the input field and therefore the wrong unit, and the language precedence read localStorage before ?lang=.
Page errors captured during the run: none.
not_benchmarked: The physiological and equipment data themselves (crew CO2/O2/moisture/heat output, sorbent capacity, scrubber efficiency, cooling COP, fan pressure rise, oxygen-generation energy, coil contact factor): these are inputs to the benchmark, not results of it. Their provenance is stated above and on the page.
The atmosphere threshold values drawn on the charts: they are teaching values, not the binding limits of any platform, and the page says so.
The schematic drawings, the object/air-path diagrams and the play/time-slider interaction.
The stored-consumables and endurance figures of the closure-comparison table, which are order-of-magnitude teaching figures.
Sorbent breakthrough behaviour, coil frosting, sorption in surfaces, stratification and transport delay: not modelled, and outside the mathematics being graded.
